title: The Thirsty Crow
pages: A crow is very thirsty.
Look! A pot with a little water.
Plop! Plop! He drops pebbles in.
The water comes up, up, up!
Glug, glug! Yum!

title: The Hare and the Tortoise
pages: Hare is fast.
Tortoise is slow.
Ready, steady, go! They race.
Hare goes to sleep. Zzz.
Tortoise wins the race!

title: The Lion and the Mouse
moral: Even the smallest friend can be a great help.
question: Who set the lion free?
The mouse
The fox
The hunter
pages: A tiny mouse ran over a sleeping lion.
The lion woke up and grabbed her. “Please let me go,” said the mouse. “One day I will help you.”
The lion laughed, but he let her go.
Later, hunters trapped the lion in a net. He roared and roared.
The mouse heard him and ran to help. She chewed the ropes with her sharp teeth.
The lion was free! Now he knew that even a small friend can help.

title: The Thirsty Crow
moral: Where there is a will, there is a way.
question: What did the crow drop in the pot?
Pebbles
Leaves
Sticks
pages: One hot day, a crow was flying everywhere looking for water.
At last he saw a pot with a little water at the bottom. His beak could not reach it.
He tried to tip the pot, but it was too heavy. Then he had an idea.
He dropped small pebbles into the pot, one by one. The water rose higher and higher.
At last the crow could drink. He was not thirsty any more.

title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
moral: Stay calm and think quickly in danger, and do not trust one who betrays a friend.
question: Where did the monkey say his heart was?
In the tree
In the river
At home
pages: A clever monkey lived in a jamun tree on a river bank. A crocodile became his friend, and the monkey shared sweet jamun fruits with him every day.
The crocodile took some fruits home to his wife. She loved them and said, “If the fruit is so sweet, the monkey’s heart must be sweeter. Bring it to me!”
The crocodile invited the monkey for a ride to his home. In the middle of the river, he told the monkey the truth.
The monkey stayed calm. “My heart is hanging on the tree,” he said. “Take me back and I will fetch it.”
The crocodile took him back. The monkey leapt up the tree and said, “Foolish friend, nobody keeps a heart on a tree. Our friendship is over!”

title: The Blue Jackal
moral: Do not pretend to be what you are not. The truth always comes out.
question: Why was the jackal found out?
He howled
He lost his crown
He fell asleep
pages: A jackal wandered into a town and dogs chased him. He jumped into a vat of blue dye to hide.
When he came out, he was blue from nose to tail! The forest animals had never seen such a creature.
“I am a special king sent to rule you,” said the jackal. The animals made him their king.
He began to ignore the other jackals and drove them away, because he felt too grand for them.
One moonlit night, jackals howled in the distance. The blue jackal forgot himself and howled along. The animals saw he was only a jackal and chased him away.
